title: Indecent Exposure
pattern: Exposing internal structs, classes, or helper methods with public visibility when they are only important for internal execution.
why_bad: It forces clients to understand and navigate internal implementation details, increasing cognitive load. It creates brittle external dependencies that prevent future internal refactoring because clients become coupled to the exposed details.
detection: Structures, methods, or traits marked with public visibility (`pub` in Rust) that are only consumed by other modules within the same crate and are never intended for downstream public use.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Public APIs and types that form the explicit, documented interface of a library or framework.
fix: Restrict visibility using fine-grained access modifiers (such as `pub(crate)` or `pub(in crate::submodule)` in Rust).
source: Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter on Smells ("Indecent Exposure"), pp. 85, 198.
